question:
(a) The radius of a nucleus is of the order of $10^{-15}\,\text{m}$. Explain why nuclear matter has very high density.
(b) A nuclear reaction has mass defect $0.020\,\text{u}$. Calculate the energy released in MeV. Take $1\,\text{u} = 931\,\text{MeV}/c^{2}$.

options.A:
(a) Nearly all atomic mass is concentrated in a nucleus of radius about $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}$, so mass per unit volume is extremely large. Since $R\propto A^{1/3}$, both nuclear mass and volume scale approximately with $A$, giving nearly constant but very high density.
(b) $E=\Delta mc^2=0.020\times931=18.62\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
options.B:
(a) Nuclear matter has low density because the nucleus occupies a large atomic volume.
(b) $E=0.020/931\approx2.15\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
options.C:
(a) Nuclear density increases directly as $A^3$ because nuclear volume is independent of $A$.
(b) $E=0.020\times931=1.862\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
options.D:
(a) Nuclear density is zero because protons and neutrons are point particles.
(b) $E=931/0.020=46550\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
